identity.title: Observational constraints on dust disk sizes in tidally truncated protoplanetary disks in multiple systems in the Taurus region

paper_type_evidence.quote: Here we present and analyze disk structures around ten multiple stellar systems that were included in an unbiased, high spatial resolution survey performed with ALMA of 32 protoplanetary disks in the Taurus star-forming region.

targets.name: Ten multiple systems in Taurus (T Tau, UY Aur, RW Aur, DK Tau, HK Tau, CIDA 9, DH Tau, V710 Tau, HN Tau, UZ Tau)

method.value: Gaia DR2 parallaxes for distances; spectral type to Teff, with luminosity, to masses via evolutionary tracks

evidence.quote: combine this with the distance corrected stellar luminosity to infer the stellar masses using the evolutionary models by (cite: baraffe15) and the nonmagnetic models by (cite: feiden16)

analysis_steps.goal: Fit continuum visibilities of each disk

method.value: Sum of axisymmetric model visibilities per component, power law with exponential cutoff (Gaussian rings for CIDA 9A, UZ Tau E); visibilities averaged per spw to one channel

evidence.quote: To fit the continuum visibilities of a multiple system made of $M$ components, we computed the total model visibilities as the sum of the visibilities of the individual components

key_parameters.value: 150 walkers, ~20000 steps (1 disk); 200 walkers, >25000 steps (2 disks); 400 walkers, 31000 steps (UZ Tau)

evidence.quote: typically we used 150 walkers and $\sim$20000 steps for the cases where only one disk is detected (8 parameters), 200 walkers and more than 25000 steps for the cases where two disks are detected (16 parameters)

assumptions.value: axisymmetric brightness profile, independent geometry per disk

evidence.quote: each disk is modeled with an independent brightness profile and geometry

fitting.value: emcee ensemble MCMC with Gaussian likelihood; medians of posterior, 16th-84th percentile uncertainties; last 3000-10000 steps used

evidence.quote: We explored the parameter space using the Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) ensemble sampler `emcee` (cite: emcee) and we adopted a Gaussian likelihood

validation.value: Reduced chi2 ~3.5 (6.4 for T Tau), attributed to CASA weights underestimated; uncertainties corrected; R_eff compared with Gaussian and Nuker profile fits

evidence.quote: We verified that the values of $R_{\rm eff,dust}$ obtained with this functional form are compatible with those obtained using a Gaussian function

method.value: R_disk,dust enclosing 95% and R_eff,dust enclosing 68% of flux; uncertainties from 1000 chains

evidence.quote: The uncertainties on these values are obtained by calculating the radii and the flux with the values obtained with 1000 different chains

analysis_steps.goal: Compare multiples with single smooth disks

method.value: Two-sided K-S tests on radii, gamma1 and gamma2 distributions vs. singles from Long et al. 2019

evidence.quote: We perform also the Kolmogorov–Smirnov (K-S) two-sided test for the null hypothesis that the samples of dust radii around single stars and around primary stars in multiple systems are drawn from the same continuous distribution.

validation.value: Repeated excluding CIDA 9A and UZ Tau E

evidence.quote: This same result is found when excluding the two disks around primary stars showing substructures (CIDA 9A and UZ Tau E)

method.value: Spherical law of cosines with fitted inclinations and position angles

evidence.quote: We computed the relative inclination of the disks in each system using the spherical law of cosines

method.value: Analytic truncation radius from Artymowicz & Lubow fit (Roche lobe times b e^c + 0.88 mu^0.01); derive minimum eccentricity for i=0 or coplanar orbit, with truncation radius = dust radius or 2x dust radius

evidence.quote: We thus explore here the eccentricities that would be derived using the measured dust disk radii as a value for the truncation radius

evidence.quote: using an estimate of the gas disk radii that is two times larger than the dust radii

claims.hypothesis: Disks in multiple systems are smaller than disks around single stars
claims.experiment: Visibility fits of 1.3 mm continuum and K-S comparison with smooth single disks
claims.result: Median R_disk,dust 21 au (primaries) vs 34 au (singles); p<1e-5
claims.finding: Dust disks in multiples are smaller

evidence.quote: we demonstrated that the disks around stars in multiple systems are smaller than in single systems in a statistically significant way

claims.hypothesis: Disk outer edges in multiples are sharper
claims.finding: Steeper outer edge, plausibly tidal truncation

evidence.quote: disks around multiple stellar systems present a statistically significant sharper outer edge in the dust emission

claims.hypothesis: Measured dust radii are consistent with tidal truncation predictions
claims.experiment: Compare R/a_p with analytic truncation models and derive minimum eccentricities
claims.result: e>0.5 in 9/11 cases if dust radius is truncation radius; reasonable if gas radius is 2x dust
claims.finding: Consistent only with high eccentricities or gas radii twice dust radii

evidence.quote: when assuming that the gas disk radii, which directly trace the dynamical truncation, are twice as large as the dust disk radii, the values of the eccentricity for the orbits are more reasonable

claims.hypothesis: Disks in a multiple system are coplanar
claims.experiment: Relative inclinations from fitted inclination and PA
claims.result: Only UZ Tau and UY Aur near 0 deg, others large

evidence.quote: Their finding that most disks in binary systems are not coplanar is reinforced here by our resolved observations

why_this_method.value: Power law with exponential cutoff chosen for better outer cutoff description than a Gaussian, one fewer parameter than Nuker, and comparability with Long et al.

evidence.quote: it has one less parameter than the Nuker profile, and the power-law exponent is not related to the exponential cutoff as it is in the similarity solution

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Gaussian, Nuker and self-similar profiles were considered; Gaussian and Nuker radii found compatible

evidence.quote: both the $R_{\rm eff,dust}$ and $R_{\rm disk,dust}$ values are compatible with the results obtained using a Nuker profile

limitations_admitted.value: Uncertainties likely underestimated; gamma2 and T Tau S, UY Aur B, HN Tau B poorly constrained; no gas data

evidence.quote: These uncertainties are likely underestimated.
